name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 281 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 32% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 281 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 32 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Manipur saw Kuki volunteers shot dead and five Kuki men mutilated, prompting protests in Kangpokpi and Noney and police response with tear gas and batons. In Kashmir a terror financing probe linked to LeT led authorities to search four locations, and an Indian national was killed in an attack on a commercial vessel off Oman. A Tata Sumo crash in Ramban killed one person and injured two, while the Supreme Court received a bail petition from Yumlembam Jiban Singh, accused of parading Kuki women naked. The UCDP recorded 437 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Manipur så Kuki-frivillige skutt og fem Kuki-menn lemlestet, noe som førte til protester i Kangpokpi og Noney og politirespons med tåregass og batonger. I Kashmir førte en terrorfinansieringsundersøkelse knyttet til LeT til at myndighetene søkte fire lokasjoner, og en indisk nasjonal ble drept i et angrep på et handelsskip utenfor Oman. En Tata-Sumo-ulykke i Ramban drepte én person og såret to, mens Høyesterett mottok en kausjonssøknad fra Yumlembam Jiban Singh, anklaget for å ha partert Kuki-kvinner nakne. UCDP registrerte 437 kamprelaterte dødsfall i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
